statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: CIPC e-Services Company Name Reservation Module (https://www.cipc.co.za)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A company name may be expressed in any of the 11 official South African languages or English. The name must be rendered in the Latin alphabet for the commercial register; non-Latin scripts require an official transliteration into English or Afrikaans. The proposed name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name or protected trade mark and must not contain prohibited or misleading terms.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A reserved name remains valid for two years from the date of CIPC approval; if the company is not incorporated within that period, a new reservation application must be filed. Upon rejection of a proposed name, the applicant may file an administrative review application with the Companies Tribunal under section 164 of the Companies Act, supported by an affidavit and documentary grounds demonstrating that the name is not prohibited or too similar to existing names. The Tribunal may extend the statutory filing period for good cause. Re-application is the ordinary remedy for managing lapsed reservations.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office may supply the statutory registered address for service, but the operational airline in-flight catering kitchen must maintain a dedicated physical facility at or near a licensed South African airport, approved by Airports Company South Africa, SARS for bonded factory / customs purposes, the Department of Agriculture, Land Reform and Rural Development, the Department of Health, and the applicable food safety authority. A virtual office cannot satisfy the commercial substance, customs bond, aviation security, or food production requirements of this industry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High; approximately 90% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by SARS, Port Health, Airports Company South Africa security, or the Department of Health within the first twelve months of operations, with recurring monthly-to-quarterly inspection exposure thereafter.

incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (MoI) adopted in terms of section 15 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a Proprietary Limited Company; shares may be issued for nil or nominal consideration and no escrow account or capital deposit account is required by the CIPC.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) the incorporation and allotment of 100 ordinary shares in favour of each subscribing incorporator be ratified, issued fully paid in accordance with the Memorandum of Incorporation; (2) the registered office be fixed at Flight 1, Aviation Park, 27 Boeing Road, Kempton Park, Gauteng, 1619, South Africa; (3) Ms. Naledi Mokoena be appointed Managing Director, Mr. Pieter Venter sole Director, and Ms. Zinhle Dube Company Secretary, each with immediate effect; (4) the Directors are vested with unrestricted authority to open banking accounts, register at SARS for income tax/VAT/PAYE/UIF/SDL, and execute all ancillary formalities required to obtain the operational licenses of the catering kitchen.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Name Reservation before the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to CIPC e-Services, complete the 'Reserve a Name' form (CoR 9.1) with up to four alternative names in priority order, upload the name-search confirmation, and settle the ZAR 125 filing fee online. No notarization is required at the pre-filing stage.
required_dossiers: CIPC name search receipt showing proposed names are available
Certified identity copies of each founding director and shareholder
Proof of intended business street address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or treated as objectionable, a formal objection or re-submission must be filed through CIPC transactional services within 10 business days; alternative names contained in the original priority list may be activated automatically.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Memorandum of Incorporation and Director Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporators and founding directors; CIPC prescribed forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the MoI using the standard CIPC template (CoR 14.1B) incorporating permissive provisions for board quorum, share classes, and special resolutions; all incorporators and each consented director must sign the CoR 14.1A director consent form; forms executed outside South Africa must be notarially certified and apostilled.
required_dossiers: Consent to Act as Director (Form CoR 14.1A) for each director
Affidavit or certificate confirming the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC raises form non-compliance queries during filing, the applicant must respond via the resubmission function within 20 business days or the application lapses; a fresh filing fee applies thereafter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Notice of Incorporation and Statutory Registration with CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), Corporate Registration Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Electronically lodge the CoR 14.1 together with the MoI in PDF format through CIPC e-Services transactional filing, pay the ZAR 425 registration fee, and obtain the electronic CSR (company registration number) and registration certificate upon approval.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where an application is 'rejected', deficiencies are corrected by filing an amended CoR 14.1 within 40 business days; erroneous refusals may be challenged through the Companies Tribunal or on judicial review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Governance Filings and Statutory Register Maintenance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC Beneficial Ownership Filings; Company Secretary of the (Pty) Ltd
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 10 business days after incorporation and upon any subsequent change, submit the beneficial ownership declaration (BBO) to CIPC and maintain the statutory registers (members, directors, auditors, securities, minutes) at the registered office in compliance with sections 24-26 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008.
required_dossiers: Register of directors and prescribed officers
Minute book containing the first board resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Non-compliance attracts administrative penalties; late or inaccurate BBO filings are remedied by an accelerated correction filing with an explanatory note and, where applicable, by responding to a CIPC compliance notice within the stated deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SARS Revenue Account Registration for Corporate Tax Obligations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 21 business days of incorporation, register the company on SARS eFiling for income tax, VAT (where taxable supplies exceed or are expected to exceed ZAR 1 million), PAYE, UIF, and SDL; upload the incorporation certificate and MoI; obtain a taxpayer reference number and registered VAT/PAYE numbers.
required_dossiers: Proof of physical address (municipal levy account or lease agreement)
Certified identity documents of all directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: SARS verification queries are managed via eFiling correspondence; blocked accounts are cleared by filing nil returns and submitting outstanding compliance declarations through a SARS branch or via the registered tax practitioner.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Corporate Bank Account under FICA Onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Major South African banks (Standard Bank, First National Bank, Absa, Nedbank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a dedicated corporate business account by presenting certified company documents, beneficial ownership disclosures, and the board resolution appointing authorised signatories; account activation follows full Financial Intelligence Centre Act (FICA) verification of all beneficial owners.
required_dossiers: Memorandum of Incorporation and first board resolution
Certified identity documents of directors and authorised signatories
Proof of registered office physical address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank issues a FICA verification query or 'suspicious' hold, the applicant must submit corrected beneficial ownership information and supporting source-of-funds evidence before a fresh account opening application is processed.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) — eFiling portal at https://efiling.sars.gov.za
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A company incorporated as a (Pty) Ltd is a South African tax resident and must obtain an income tax reference number by registering with SARS through eFiling or a SARS branch. For VAT, a vendor must register within 21 days of exceeding the R1,000,000 annual turnover threshold or earlier if compulsory registration applies. Non-resident foreign entities deriving South African-source income must register separately as a foreign company or foreign investment entity, appoint a public officer, and obtain a SARS income tax reference number; a separate VAT vendor number is required if taxable supplies exceed the registration threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa does not operate a US-style check-the-box election. A (Pty) Ltd is taxed at entity level on worldwide income, with distributions subject to dividends withholding tax. Binding private rulings may be obtained from SARS to clarify the classification of hybrid instruments and hybrid mismatch arrangements; anti-avoidance re-characterisation rules in sections 8E, 8EA, 8EB and the General Anti-Avoidance Rule may override contractual labels, but no elective entity pass-through regime is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the South African Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Africa does not currently mandate real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or continuous transaction controls. SARS requires a valid VAT invoice containing the prescribed particulars under section 20(1) of the VAT Act, issued within 21 days of the supply. SARS eFiling provides an API-based channel for submitting VAT returns and declarations; electronic invoicing is permissible but no mandatory government-side clearance or e-invoicing database requirement is in force.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported from South Africa within the prescribed period qualify for the zero rate under section 11(1)(a) of the VAT Act if documentary proof of export is retained. Services supplied to non-residents and not used in South Africa may qualify under section 11(2). For airline inflight catering, zero rating may apply to supplies consumed outside South Africa on international flights where the goods are securely exported and supported by international carrier documentation; supplies for domestic flights remain taxable at 15%.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or unsupported export zero-rating claims attract an understatement penalty of up to 200% of the tax shortfall plus interest under the Tax Administration Act. False customs declarations and false VAT certificates may trigger criminal liability, fines of up to R1,000,000, and imprisonment under the Customs and Excise Act. SARS may retrospectively claw back the zero-rated VAT, impose additional tax, and deny refunds where export documentation, physical movement, or the 180-day foreign currency repatriation condition is not substantiated to SARS's satisfaction.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) acting through the Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), operating under the Currency and Exchanges Manual for Authorised Dealers, supported by the Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC) for AML/CFT supervision and SARS for tax clearance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South African Rand (ZAR) is freely convertible for genuine current-account transactions, including trade settlement, operational expenditures, branch remittances, and dividends, provided the Authorised Dealer obtains the relevant supporting documentation and, where applicable, SARS tax clearance. Capital-account flows (equity subscriptions, shareholder loans, foreign direct investment, and outward investment) remain subject to regulated reporting and notification to SARB FinSurv through an Authorised Dealer. For a non-resident-owned ZA (Pty) Ltd, each inward foreign direct investment (FDI) transfer must be registered with the receiving bank so that the corresponding historic inward reference is recorded; this record creates (a) the ability to remit dividends, (b) the ability to repatriate capital on disinvestment, and (c) a compliant route for intercompany finance. Profit remittance hurdles: dividend payments require a valid SARS dividend withholding tax declaration or treaty-based withholding rate reduction; the remitting bank must observe Dividend Withholding Tax (DWT) compliance at 20% (or reduced rate under an applicable double-taxation agreement). No corporate-level exchange control approval is needed for an ordinary dividend remittance where the entity is in a tax-compliance position and the underlying capital was lawfully brought into South Africa through a registered inward route. The ZAR trades on a free float, so conversion risk is systematic rather than regulatory.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export earnings from South African goods and services, including inflight-catering meals and bonded kitchen supplies sold to foreign-domiciled airlines, must be paid into South Africa through an Authorised Dealer within 180 days from the date of export (extendable to 365 days with SARB FinSurv approval for capital items or long-dated trade contracts). The proceeds must be credited to a ZAR account of the exporting entity, surrendering foreign currency to the domestic market; there is no fixed-rate/conversion-free choice under a floating-exchange-rate regime, but the transaction must be reported via the balance-of-payments (BOP) reporting system. The exporter must retain the SARS-specific export declaration, customs entry (SAD500), airline pro-forma invoice/purchase order, and a certificate of export where border controls apply. In practice, the receivables must match the declared invoice values and no netting with intercompany payables may occur without prior Authorised Dealer approval.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility as the sole primary treasury rail. Offshore digital EMIs, virtual payment service providers, and non-resident fintechs are not recognised as Authorised Dealers under SARB's Currency and Exchanges Manual and cannot legally process the inward FDI registration required for the repatriation of capital or for conversion of export proceeds. Such EMIs may only be used as ancillary receivables/payment facilitators for low-value, non-core transactions; they must never hold the main contractual account, the capital escrow account, or the SARB-notifiable international transfer channels. A fully locally-regulated niche EMI (e.g., a licensed forex subdivision or payment-service-oriented B2B provider) could play a limited role for small-ticket supplier payments in the SADC region, provided the principal treasury remains a South African banking counterparty. Alternative fintech bridge model: use the EMI solely to execute domestic ZAR ACH disbursements to local staff/suppliers and house the international remittance clearing through an authorised dealer.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Yes, physical presence is generally mandatory for at least one member of the board or a formally-authorised Company Secretary/Compliance Officer during account opening at most tier-1 South African banks. The FICA (Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001) accountable-institution rules requires the bank to obtain certified copies of directors' passports, proof of residential address for each 10% shareholder, and a board resolution with a clear authorized signature list. A remote-video KYC interview is only accepted where (i) the company is already registered in CIPC, (ii) the beneficial owner is available for live audiovisual identification, (iii) the originals are certified by a notary / embassy, and (iv) the relationship is rated low risk. Given the common use of offshore parent companies and foreign directors for airline catering ventures, the most reliable onboarding path is to appoint one local resident director / independent compliance signatory, present that individual physically at the bank branch, and hold the overseas beneficial-owner KYC materials ready for the mandated 'who is behind the company' completion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign-resident beneficial owners with a recently formed South African (Pty) Ltd and no prior audited financial statements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Company MOI, CIPC certificate, beneficial ownership register extracts, passport and proof-of-address certificates of all natural persons, corporate structure chart with ultimate beneficiary identification, source-of-funds documentation (wealth accumulation evidence, e.g., tax returns, dividends, salary slips), and board resolution providing the bank with signed copies of the proposed aviation catering master service agreements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume export receipts from invoice-based airline contracts, triggering questions about trade-based money laundering risk in a bond/airport context
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed airline purchase orders; IATA-specific catering liason contracts; aircraft turnaround and ramp access permits; SARB export declaration forms and customs export entries; invoice-to-payment reconciliation ledger; comprehensive HAACP/food-safety certificates; and a standard internal audit pack containing the underlying transport, storage, and sanitary compliance documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intercompany/intra-group funding patterns mixing equity and shareholder loans, causing thin-cap and exchange-control scrutiny
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully documented intercompany loan agreements bearing arm's-length interest rate proofs; source funds from bank statements and tax-compliant corporate records; calculation of Section 23N interest deduction limits; section 31 OECD-consistent transfer-pricing report; board-approved funding strategy; and an explanatory memorandum to the Authorised Dealer confirming the round-trip of any retained bearings in an inward FDI notification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Appearance on screening lists or adverse-media flags for a shareholder or related supply-chain entity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Global sanctions screening reports (OFAC, EU, UN, HM Treasury, and FIC lists); independent PEP/PEP-adjacency evaluation; court-paper dissolution, litigation, and insolvency certificates; notarised professional reference letters from a regulated auditor/lawyer; and an affidavit explaining the nexus between the subject entity and the catering kitchen.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The preferred route is a direct SWIFT MT103/MT202 from the non-resident shareholder's bank to the South African corporate account at the chosen Authorised Dealer. Field 70 must explicitly contain the purpose code 'FDI Equity Contribution' or 'SA Share Subscription', reference the new beneficiary company name and share subscription agreement, and state 'CZ — Capital Transfer, No Inward Foreign Investment Certification Required - Authorised Dealer to file the inward formal notification'. The Authorised Dealer is obligated to obtain supporting documentation (share subscription resolution, allotment letter, international transaction report, and exchange-control controls) and will assign a unique 'inward foreign investment notification' reference. For funds coming as shareholder loans rather than equity, the same routing must state 'CS — Foreign Bank Credit Facility' or a specific 'import/working-capital' narrative that avoids misclassification of a loan as revenue; a formal loan agreement, commercial rate certificate, and a SARB record of outward financing capacity will be required for future interest and principal repatriation. Directors and shareholders must avoid using personal accounts for corporate capital injection; all inbound FDI must be wired directly into the corporate operational account, with no interposition of intermediaries, payment wallets, or digital foreign currency platforms.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade disbursements from the South African catering kitchen will separate into (i) local domestic expenditure in ZAR cleared via the South African national payments system (EPG/ACH) and electronically transferred from the operational ZAR account, and (ii) international obligations (e.g., imported food-grade packaging, airline invoices, equipment leases, frozen goods imported from the EU or Asia) sent through the International Payments network by SWIFT MT103 using explicit underlying commercial invoice and customs reference details. For larger aviation contract disbursements, a documentary letter of credit via MT700/MT707 would, in rare cases, be used if the airline requires proof for supplies at hub stations; practically, monthly ACH/ZAR-wire settlement from the client's South African treasury to the operational account is the core rail for receivables, while the outbound to third-party international suppliers is typically structured using payment-on-delivery instructions with netting restrictions. All outward remittances require completion of the Authorised Dealer's BOP code, and invoices above the threshold must be supported by a SARS eFiling-generated Import/Export registration and customs declarations. The company should maintain a 'forex facilitation file' containing purchase orders, invoices, air waybills, customs clearances, and proof-of-payment to facilitate custom requests. For Intra-SACU flows (Namibia, Botswana, Eswatini, Lesotho), funds can be cleared via SACU/CMA arrangements with local payment system participant banks, thereby avoiding mere SWIFT costs and allowing ACH-like direct transfers.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards (standard ZAR/USD, ZAR/EUR, ZAR/GBP) with a documented underlying foreign currency exposure arising from the supply of inflight-catering meals and the payment of importable raw materials.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) transacted offshore or through non-South African counterparties, permitted only where the Authorised Dealer has confirmed a real economic exposure and where liquidity is sourced outside the domestic exchange-control constrains.

FX Swaps / Cross-Currency Swaps, used for aligning the timing of monthly US-dominated aviation contract receivables with the USD-denominated input costs of global food supply chains, subject to the provision that the Greek underlying is evidenced by actual trade flow documentation.

Currency Options (vanilla ZAR call/put) acquired via a licensed Authorised Dealer, recommended for large airline contract tender currency exposure at an affordable premium and capped under the standard exchange-control 'underlying commercial need' rule.

Interest-rate-FX combined swap structures (e.g., cross-currency interest-rate swaps) permissible under SARB guidelines, but they must be effected exclusively through the corporate Authorised Dealer and integrated into the bank's treasury facility documentation, with supporting audited financial statements for the exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Annual Return (AR) — Companies Act 2008 s33 and Companies Regulation 34
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), e-Services portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Tiered monthly late penalty of R50–R600 depending on turnover/assets class until filed; company flagged as 'in arrears'; CIPC issues demand, then 30-day notice of proposed deregistration under s82(3); final strike-off transfers undistributed assets to the State as bona vacantia.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (IFRS) — board approval and presentation to shareholders at the AGM
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders at the Annual General Meeting; minutes retained in statutory minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the financial year end (s30 and s61(7)(d)); a 28/29 February year-end company holds the AGM by 31 August.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors commit a reportable contravention; CIPC compliance notice and court order may follow; company cannot obtain a good-standing certificate; dividend distributions prohibited until AFS are approved.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of audited annual financial statements with CIPC under s33A (Companies Amendment Act 2024) applying to companies with Public Interest Score ≥ 350
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), electronic AFS repository
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of the financial year (s33A, in force 27 December 2024); a 28/29 February year-end company files by 31 August.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory offence under the Companies Act; CIPC compliance notice and administrative penalties; company loses good-standing status and directors remain exposed while default continues.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (ITR14) and supporting schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the end of the financial year (a 28/29 February year-end return is due by the following 28/29 February).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late payment penalty (TAA s210) plus interest at the prescribed rate (repo rate + 3%); understatement penalties up to 140% of the shortfall (TAA ss222–224); criminal prosecution for repeated or wilful non-compliance (TAA s235).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership (UBO) register maintenance, change filing, and annual return confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), beneficial ownership filing module
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Any change in beneficial ownership filed with CIPC within 30 days of the change; currency of UBO data confirmed when the annual return is submitted (no standalone calendar-year re-filing).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Offence under the Companies Act as amended by the General Laws (AML/CFT) Amendment Act 22 of 2022 — fine and/or imprisonment of directors; CIPC blocks annual return processing until UBO register is current.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Compulsory independent audit by a Registered Auditor where the Public Interest Score (PIS) is ≥ 350, or for any public/state-owned company, or where the MOI requires it. PIS is computed under Companies Regulation 26(2): 1 point per employee; 1 point per R1 million of third-party liabilities; 1 point per R1 million of turnover; 1 point per shareholder. An inflight catering kitchen with 250+ employees and R150m+ turnover scores well above 350, so a full audit is the prudent assumption. Companies with PIS of 100–349 require an independent review (Regulation 28).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB is mandatory for companies with PIS ≥ 350 and for public/state-owned companies; private companies with PIS < 350 may elect IFRS for SMEs (Financial Reporting Standards framework under Companies Act s29(4)).

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (companies and close corporations; rate for years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023; 28% for prior years)
